newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's first lady figures in police course.
newsitem.headline: Israel's first lady figures in police course.

text.p: Israeli police are learning about taking suspects' words at face value by studying first lady Sara Netanyahu's expressions in a television interview, a behavioural sciences instructor said on Thursday.

Gavriel Raam, who lectures police on non-verbal signals, told Reuters he uses the interview with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's wife because her facial expressions indicate "she is trying to hide something".

Shai Bazak, the prime minister's spokesman, dismissed as "nonsense" the report of the special police training, first published on Thursday in Israel's newspaper Haaretz. "I don't want to comment on that," he told Reuters.
In the interview with Israel's Channel Two television last July, Netanyahu was asked about her widely publicised dismissal of her children's nanny.
The nanny told the press she was humiliated before being tossed out of the house.

"Asked if the nanny scandal bothered her, Sara said no. But at the same moment she swallowed her lower lip. When a person says a word and swallows their lip it means they have a problem with what they just said," Raam said.

In the interview, Netanyahu was also asked about her feelings towards Susan Amor, the wife of a Likud party legislator who has complained bitterly that the prime minister reneged on a promise to appoint him speaker of parliament.
"Sara says she has no problem with Amor but at that very moment, she bites both lips and sticks out her tongue," Raam said.
